Map authority axis directions to project API fields

Verify independent control points and both Excel axis orders

issues.details: Paper C1: longitude 21.95, east shift 1250000. EPSG C0: longitude 21.95, false easting 250000. EPSG C1: longitude 24.95, false easting 1250000. Same district/zone label is insufficient to identify the projection.

EPSG C uses latitude of origin 0.1 degrees and false northing 0; EPSG X uses latitude of origin 5/60 degrees and false northing 0. Precisely lists C-like KS-1963 with latitude origin 0 and false northing -11057.63, with a Lithuanian datum variant. Published positive north shifts must not be copied directly into PROJ y_0. Do not combine parameters from different representations.
EPSG:7831 defines X7; the observed geoproj list contains X1–X6. The original source list is preserved.
Authority definitions also include A1–A4, K2–K4 and C0, absent from the observed geoproj catalogue. The 18 geoproj variants are not a complete SK-63 registry.

GIS-Lab describes a fixed standard width per district and alternate-width use; the 2021 paper describes mixed widths for the 60N-crossing group. Geoproj exposes W3 and W6. Preserve both variants; neither label establishes the standard width or projection parameters.
The linked giscraft grid page now serves unrelated content. No grid or parameter data were obtained from it.

validation.method: Centre of each EPSG area bounding box, EPSG:4284 to projected CRS and back, always_xy=True, no datum transformation.
validation.note: Self-consistency check only; not evidence of geoproj equivalence or absolute accuracy.

gis_lab_findings.alternate_width_rule: Alternate-width meridians retain the standard alignment and become denser or sparser. The article supplies no anchor longitude or alternate numbering formula.
